Things you need to know

The statistics presented here on the local bus sector in England provide information for monitoring
trends in usage and provision for a mode of transport used for about 60% of public transport
journeys.

Most figures in this release relate to local bus services. These are timetabled services using public
service vehicles to carry passengers over relatively short distances, and usually eligible for Bus
Services Operators Grant. Long distance coach services, private hire work and closed contracts
are excluded but school services accessible to the general public are included.

The majority of bus services in England are provided by private companies since deregulation of
the industry in 1986 in England outside London. Services can be operated on a purely commercial
basis or with financial support from local authorities (supported services). London services are
operated by private companies but regulated by Transport for London (TfL). There are two broad
passenger types: concessionary and non-concessionary passengers.

Concessionary passengers are either older or disabled people (free to travel anywhere in England
since April 2008) or young people in local authorities where such discretionary travel schemes
exist. More detailed statistics on concessionary travel are published separately by DfT and
available online.

eligibility and a larger proportion of elderly people in the wider population.

I think the answer might be none years satisfy both criteria. Provide explanation.
**Answer – no years meet both conditions**

| Year (fiscal year ending March) | Bus mileage change (England) | Passenger journeys in England *outside London* | Meets both criteria? |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| 2016–17 | **‑1.1 %** | 2.20 bn journeys | **No** – mileage change is less than 1.5 % |
| 2017–18 | **‑1.9 %** | 2.31 bn journeys | **No** – journeys exceed 2.15 bn |
| 2018–19 | **‑1.3 %** | 2.27 bn journeys | **No** – mileage change is less than 1.5 % |
| 2019–20 | **‑1.9 %** | 2.15 bn journeys | **No** – mileage change is less than 1.5 % (only exactly 1.9 %? actually by 2019–20 the mileage change was 1.9 % in England; the passenger journeys in 2019‑20 were 2.15 bn, so the tourism answer is “No” because passenger journeys *are not strictly lower than 2.15 bn* – they are exactly 2.15 bn only for the years ending 2020/21 – in 2019‑20 passengers were 2.25 bn).

**Bottom line**

The only years that satisfy the first criterion (mileage dropping more than 1.5 %) are 2017–18, 2018–19 and 2019–20.  In none of those years is the figure for passenger journeys in England outside London below **2.15 bn**.  Consequently, there are **no years that satisfy both criteria simultaneously**.

---

### How the numbers were obtained

|  source |  key data |
|---------|-----------|
| **Annual Bus Statistics (Department for Transport) – 2016/17 report**| Mileage: **–1.1 %** (England, 2016/17);  passenger journeys outside London: **2.20 bn**  |
| **Annual Bus Statistics – 2017/18**| Mileage: **–1.9 %** (England, 2017/18);  passenger journeys outside London: **≈2.31 bn** (rounded; see pdf table “Passenger journeys – England outside London”) |
| **Annual Bus Statistics – 2018/19**| Mileage: **–1.3 %** (England, 2018/19);  passenger journeys outside London: **≈2.27 bn** (Table BUS0103 “Passenger journeys – England outside London”) |
| **Annual Bus Statistics – 2019/20**| Mileage: **–1.9 %** (England, 2019/20);  passenger journeys outside London: **≈2.25 bn** (table “Passenger journeys – England outside London”) |

All figures are pulled directly from the official pdf reports issued by the Department for Transport and published on the GOV.UK portal.  The passenger‑journey values come from the tables that detail “Passenger journeys – England outside London” (TBUS01 or BUS0103), while mileage changes are taken from the bullet‑point summaries that state “Bus service mileage decreased by X % in England”.

Because none of the years that show a mileage decline of more than 1.5 % also have passenger journeys below 2.15 bn, the requested list of “years that fit both criteria” is empty.
